title: MyRecon OSINT Suite: Breach, DNS & IP Modules | MyRecon
description: Explore MyRecon features: control-verified username sweeps, email breach lookups, k-anonymity password checks, RDAP domain, DNS and IP tools.
h1: OSINT modules for public profile, breach and DNS audits
intro: MyRecon combines public username lookup with email, breach, password, domain, DNS and IP checks. This guide explains what each feature examines, where its data comes from, and how to interpret uncertain results. Use the live tool and current plan details to confirm access and scope.

sections.heading: Username lookup across public profiles
sections.body:
Search a username you own or are authorized to review. MyRecon checks supported public profile pages and reports candidates for manual verification. Guest scans preview 100 sites (up to 5 results shown in full); sign in for 560+ platform standard sweeps or 3,000+ Extended coverage on Pro plans.

Coverage changes by platform, and MyRecon classifies responses using HTTP semantics (RFC 9110) plus response-body signals so a blocked request or login wall stays unknown rather than being counted as a match. Numeric Discord IDs are decoded and checked separately through Discord's public API documentation model.

sections.heading: Email and breach exposure
sections.body:
Email checks examine provider and deliverability signals, disposable-address indicators, public profile records such as Gravatar JSON profiles, optional Holehe-style registration signals, and available breach exposure from public breach sources modeled after the Have I Been Pwned API v3 schema.

A breach result describes data in a source record; it does not prove that an account is currently compromised. Review the affected fields and follow the remediation guidance for the account you control.

sections.heading: Password exposure checks
sections.body: The password exposure checker hashes the password in your browser and uses the first five characters of that SHA-1 hash for a Pwned Passwords k-anonymity lookup. The password itself is not sent to MyRecon. Use a password you control, and change it anywhere it is reused if the check reports exposure.

sections.heading: Domain registration and DNS
sections.body:
Domain lookups use RDAP (RFC 7480), the modern registration-data protocol that succeeds WHOIS for many registries, to show available registrar, registration, and nameserver details. DNS lookups resolve records such as A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT, CNAME, SOA, and CAA using DNS-over-HTTPS (RFC 8484).

Public registration records can be redacted, and DNS answers describe current configuration rather than who controls a service.

sections.heading: IP address context
sections.body: IP checks can show approximate geolocation, network or ASN ownership, hosting indicators, and reverse DNS when those public sources return data. Geolocation is approximate and usually identifies a network endpoint, not a person's home or precise location. A proxy or hosting flag is one signal, not a judgment about intent.

sections.heading: Review, export, and privacy
sections.body: Open candidate links at their original sources before relying on a result. Search inputs and results are not saved on MyRecon servers; results remain in your current browser session, and any explicit local saves or exported files stay under your control. Read the privacy policy for current retention and account metadata details.

sections.heading: Use MyRecon within its limits
sections.body: MyRecon works with public sources and cannot open private accounts or restricted material. A matching username is a lead, not proof of identity, and an empty result is not proof that an account does not exist. Use the tools for your own footprint or an authorized review, and keep the original source and uncertainty with any notes you retain.

method: Module behavior and data-handling statements were verified against MyRecon's privacy policy and primary technical references (RFC 9110, RFC 7480, RFC 8484, Have I Been Pwned API v3 and Pwned Passwords, Discord Developer Docs, Gravatar JSON Docs, and Holehe), checked 28 Nov 2026.

faq.question: What can I check with MyRecon?
faq.answer: MyRecon includes public username, email and breach, password exposure, domain registration, DNS, and IP checks. Coverage and access can vary by tool, so use the live interface and current plan page to confirm what is available.

faq.question: Does a missing username result prove no account exists?
faq.answer: No. A site may block, rate-limit, rename, or restrict a profile, and some services may not be supported. Treat an unavailable or missing result as inconclusive unless the source provides a verifiable reason.

faq.question: Can MyRecon confirm that a profile belongs to a person?
faq.answer: No. A matching username is only a lead. Confirm important conclusions with independent public evidence and keep uncertain links unconfirmed. MyRecon does not access private accounts or restricted content.

faq.question: Is the password exposure check private?
faq.answer: The browser hashes the password and sends only the first five characters of the hash for the k-anonymity check. The password itself is not sent to MyRecon. See the privacy policy for details about data handling.

product_claims: MyRecon supports a public username lookup workflow for checks available through its current platform catalogue; individual sites can be unavailable or change their behavior.
A result is a candidate for manual verification, not proof that a named person controls an account or that no account exists when no result appears.
